transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, HarborEdge), Liam O'Neill (Head of ML), Ravi Kumar (Lead DevOps)

Summary:
High-level discovery for Redwood Dedicated capacity. HarborEdge is evaluating reserved GPUs for low-latency customer-facing features, needs strong isolation and the ability to burst to hosted when seasonality spikes. Key constraints: PCI-related data residency, on-prem networking, and predictable cost model. Next steps: Redwood to run a benchmark plan and share pricing/SOW/security docs.

Topics: current infra, isolation requirements, burst/fallback strategy, scaling expectations, security/compliance, high-level pricing signals

Action items (recap): see metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we will kick off with a quick intro then Samir will do the technical questions.
[00:12] Maya: hi thanks, Maya here, CTO at HarborEdge, Liam and Ravi are on, excited to talk through dedicated capacity.
[00:18] Liam: morning all, quick note - we run a mix of on-prem k8s + some cloud for analytics, currently 8x A100s across two clusters.
[00:28] Ravi: yep, DevOps here, our network egress is tightly controlled, and any external connections must go through our proxy and jumpbox.
[00:36] Samir: perfect, thanks. so first question, what's the main workload you expect? is it chat generation, embeddings, or batch inferencing?
[00:45] Maya: primarily chat for our customer support assistant, low latency is critical. embeddings for search will be batch overnight. also a small reranker flow.
[00:55] Jordan: good, and can you share target SLOs? e.g. p95/p99 latency, concurrent users?
[01:02] Liam: target is p99 generation under 250ms for single-turn chat under normal load, and we're planning for 1,000 concurrent active sessions at peak.
[01:12] Samir: ok that helps. for Dedicated we usually size reserved GPU pools based on throughput targets. have you thought about model family / quantization? are you open to 8-bit quantized variants to reduce cost?
[01:24] Maya: we're model-agnostic atm, but we need to keep quality tight. any quantization has to be validated against our eval prompts. quality regressions are a big no.
[01:34] Liam: also, we need token accounting per customer for billing, so request-level metadata capture is needed.
[01:42] Samir: understood. Redwood Dedicated supports per-route logging and token breakdowns, and our runtime can annotate requests for downstream billing.
[01:50] Ravi: security - we are PCI scoped and the data flow for some customer interactions contains payment tokens, so isolation and key management are essential. we cannot have shared host-level volumes with other tenants.
[02:03] Jordan: yep that's a common ask. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and we can run in a VPC / private deployment model. we also have an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[02:14] Maya: we prefer a Redwood-managed control plane but private networking to our VPC. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations?
[02:23] Samir: yes, we integrate with customer KMS providers for key wrapping; HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments - for Dedicated in cloud we can support KMS encryption and bring-your-own-key. we'll share the security whitepaper.
[02:36] Liam: can you describe the burst strategy? some months we have massive spikes for promos, we need to burst beyond reserved capacity without losing requests.
[02:46] Samir: we have two patterns: burst within Dedicated via autoscaling pools (if you reserve headroom), or automated routing/fallback to hosted instances when Dedicated is saturated. fallback preserves requests, though latency might be higher depending on region and model variant.
[03:00] Ravi: how does routing work? is that a live policy we can control?
[03:05] Samir: yes, smart routing policies - you can route by latency, cost, or region. you can also define automatic fallback thresholds and per-route fallback targets, e.g., if p99 > 300ms for 30s then route new requests to hosted.
[03:19] Maya: will hosted run our same model, or a variant? data residency matters. for PCI flows we can't leave region X.
[03:27] Jordan: hosted region constraints are a thing - we can host in specific regions, but for sensitive PCI paths we recommend Dedicated or Private with VPC peering. hosted fallback is typically to a compatible model variant in the same region if available, otherwise the fallbacks are subject to region availability.
[03:44] Liam: latency-wise will fallback push us over SLOs?
[03:48] Samir: depends. fallback is intended to keep service online; it may increase latency a bit, and that's why many customers use canary rollouts and staged fallbacks. we can provision burst capacity on Dedicated (temporary reserve) for known events - that is part of the commercial discussion.
[04:03] Ravi: what about the KV cache and prefix caching? we heavily rely on kv cache for multi-turn sessions. any compatibility issues? i've seen docs call it KV cache, sometimes KV cash in transcripts, ha.
[04:15] Samir: yes continuous KV cache is supported and we can preserve per-session caches on dedicated pools. our runtime manages cache sharding; we can discuss cache warm-up strategies in the benchmark.
[04:26] Maya: benchmarks - what do you need from us to run an accurate test?
[04:30] Samir: sample prompts, typical sequence length distribution, QPS targets, and access to a small test key or synthetic traffic script. we'll run p99/p95 latency tests and throughput curves with your model variants or one of our verified open models.
[04:43] Liam: we will provide a 2-week window of traffic capture and a set of 500 eval prompts.
[04:48] Jordan: perfect. i'll include that in the next steps.
[04:52] Maya: pricing - we are sensitive to committed vs burst pricing. can you give an early ballpark?
[04:58] Jordan: high-level, Dedicated is reserved GPU pricing with options for burst credits or pay-as-you-go top-up for hosted fallback. i'll send a matrix showing examples: e.g., 8x A100 reserved vs 16x reserved with burst pool and the expected cost per 1M tokens. it's indicative until we finalize sizing from the benchmark.
[05:18] Ravi: SLA expectations - we need 99.9% uptime and defined latency SLAs. do you do per-tenant SLAs?
[05:25] Samir: dedicated instances come with SLA-backed uptime and we can negotiate latency targets for enterprise contracts. SLA exceptions, maintenance windows, and rollback policies are documented in the SOW.
[05:37] Maya: compliance - do you have SOC 2 certs, ISO, and do you produce audit logs with token metadata redaction?
[05:45] Jordan: we are SOC 2 compliant, we have ISO in progress, and our observability has token-level cost and latency breakdowns with configurable redaction. we'll send our compliance pack and security contact.
[05:58] Liam: network egress - if we peer VPCs, are we able to restrict egress to internal endpoints only?
[06:04] Samir: yes, with Private or VPC peering we can limit public egress; the control plane communicates over secure tunnels and you can require traffic through your jumpbox.
[06:13] Ravi: what about on-prem option? we might want a hybrid - control plane in Redwood managed cloud, runtime on-prem in our racks.
[06:22] Samir: that's our Private pattern - runtime can be deployed on-prem with a private control plane. there are options for air-gapped installs as well. we'll include the architecture doc link in the follow-up.
[06:32] Maya: timeline - we want a POC in about 4-6 weeks, production in 3 months if POC is successful. is that realistic?
[06:40] Jordan: yes, POC in 4-6 weeks is typical: week 1 discovery and access, week 2 benchmark runs, week 3 tuning and validation, week 4 trialing routing policies. production in 3 months depends on procurement and infra changes.
[06:53] Liam: procurement note - we need an early SOW and an example contract to start legal review.
[06:59] Jordan: understood, i'll send SOW template and sample contract redlines.
[07:03] Maya: do you have references in finance or payments? we'd like to speak to a similar customer.
[07:09] Jordan: yes, i'll connect you with another fintech customer (intro pending approval).
[07:14] Ravi: operational concerns - backup of model weights and upgrade windows, how do you handle model rollouts and canarying?
[07:23] Samir: we support canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies, and we keep model artifact snapshots with versioning. upgrades are coordinated with scheduled maintenance windows that honor your SLA.
[07:35] Liam: logging retention - how long are logs kept and can we set retention for different classes (billing vs debug)?
[07:41] Jordan: yes, retention is configurable. standard packages include 90 days, extended retention is an add-on. billing-level summaries can be retained longer while verbose debug logs can be kept for a shorter period.
[07:52] Maya: curious about autoscaling speed. if we need to scale from 8 to 16 GPUs, what's the typical time?
[07:59] Samir: scaling windows vary - for reserved Dedicated pools with pre-warmed capacity, scaling can be near-instant for routing; otherwise spinning up new VMs in cloud may take a few minutes. part of the recommendation is to maintain a small buffer to handle spikes.
[08:12] Ravi: for our use-case we want sub-2 minute response for user actions, so a couple-minutes cold spin might be risky.
[08:18] Samir: then we recommend either reserved burst capacity or hybrid strategy: reserved baseline on Dedicated plus hosted fallback configured to the same region; and conservative thresholds so you don't hit cold start windows.
[08:31] Jordan: ok quick recap - we'll: 1) run benchmark plan, 2) share dedicated pricing + SOW, 3) send security/compliance pack, 4) schedule console demo and canary design session.
[08:44] Maya: sounds good. any final questions?
[08:47] Liam: just one - do you offer sample instrumentation for token-level billing integration?
[08:51] Samir: yes, we have SDK examples and sample webhooks for token events; i'll drop a link in follow-up.
[08:59] Ravi: please make sure all external links go through our proxy domain, we'll provide the jumpbox details.
[09:04] Jordan: noted. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and timelines.
[09:10] Maya: thanks all.

(Transcript ends; timestamps approximate.)
